statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: A NAS may interface directly to a telco analog or digital circuit or attach via an external modem or terminal adapter.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: The NAS, in conjunction with the modem or terminal adapters, may perform rate adaption, analog to digital conversion, sync to async conversion or a number of other alterations of data streams.

statements.subject: pptp
statements.description: Standard PPP client software should continue to operate on tunneled PPP links.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A PAC may provide service to many PNSs.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A single PNS may associate with many PACs to concentrate traffic from a large number of geographically diverse sites.

statements.subject: pptp
statements.description: PPTP does not dictate the particular algorithms to be used for this low level control but it does define the parameters that must be communicated in order to allow such algorithms to work.

statements.subject: pptp
statements.description: It may also tunnel non-IP protocols.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Since PPTP relies completely on TCP/IP and is independent of the interface hardware, the PNS may use any combination of IP interface hardware including LAN and WAN devices.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Before PPP tunneling can occur between a PAC and PNS, a control connection must be established between them.
actions: establish control connection between PAC and PNS

statements.subject: participant
statements.description: Once the control connection is established, the PAC or PNS may initiate sessions by requesting outbound calls or responding to inbound requests.
actions: initiate session by requesting outbound call
initiate session by responding to inbound request

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The control connection may communicate changes in operating characteristics of an individual user session with a Set-Link-Info message.
actions: send Set-Link-Info message on control connection

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Individual sessions may be released by either the PAC or PNS, also through Control Connection messages.
actions: send Control Connection message to release session

statements.subject: pptp
statements.description: It should not be used as a means for resynchronizing the TCP data stream in the event that a transmitter issues an improperly formatted message.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Loss of synchronization must result in immediate closing of the control connection's TCP session.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Any "reserved" fields MUST be sent as 0 values to allow for protocol extensibility.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: A control connection must be established before any other PPTP messages can be issued.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Reserved0                This field MUST be 0.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Reserved1                This field MUST be 0.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: In Start-Control-Connection-Requests issued by the PNS, this value SHOULD be set to 0.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: It MUST be ignored by the PAC.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: If less than 64 octets in length, the remainder of this field SHOULD be filled with octets of value 0.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: This field MUST be 0.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: In a Start-Control-Connection-Reply issued by the PNS, this value SHOULD be set to 0 and it must be ignored by the PAC.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The PNS MUST NOT use this value to try to track the remaining number of PPP sessions that the PAC will allow.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Reserved1, Reserved2     These fields MUST be 0.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The combination of IP address and call serial number SHOULD be unique.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: This value should be set to the maximum delay that can normally occur between the time a packet arrives at the PAC and is delivered to the client.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: 1 (Connect) - The PAC should answer the incoming call

statements.subject: session
statements.description: 2 (General Error) - The Incoming Call should not be established due to the reason indicated in Error Code
statements.trigger: Incoming-Call-Reply received with Result Code = 2 (General Error)

statements.subject: server
statements.description: 3 (Do Not Accept) - The PAC should not accept the incoming call.
statements.trigger: Incoming-Call-Reply received with Result Code = 3 (Do Not Accept)

statements.subject: server
statements.description: It should hang up or issue a busy indication
statements.trigger: Incoming-Call-Reply received with Result Code = 3 (Do Not Accept)

statements.subject: server
statements.description: This message should only be sent when an error occurs, and not more than once every 60 seconds.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Because these options can change at any time during the life of the call, the PAC must be able to update its internal call information dynamically and perform PPP negotiation on an active PPP session.
actions: perform PPP negotiation on the active PPP session

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The send ACCM value the client should use to process outgoing PPP packets.  The default value used by the client until this message is received is 0XFFFFFFFF.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The receive ACCM value the client should use to process incoming PPP packets. The default value used by the client until this message is received is 0XFFFFFFFF.

statements.subject: participant
statements.description: If a PPTP reply indicates in its Result Code that a general error occurred, the General Error value should be examined to determined what the error was.
actions: examine General Error field of reply to determine specific error cause

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The TCP connection itself, however, can close at any time and an appropriate error recovery mechanism must be provided to handle this case.
actions: initiate error recovery mechanism upon TCP connection closure

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Appropriate logging should be implemented for easy determination of the problems and the reasons for closing the control connection.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Receipt of an invalid or malformed Control Connection message should be logged appropriately, and the control connection should be closed and restarted to ensure recovery into a known state.
actions: log receipt of invalid or malformed Control Connection message

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: If the version of the reply is lower than the version sent in the request, the older (lower) version should be used provided it is supported.
statements.trigger: Start-Control-Connection-Reply received with lower supported version
statements.pre_cond: protocol.state = wait_ctl_reply & reply.version < request.version & reply.version.supported = true
actions: Use the older (lower) version from the reply

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: If the version is earlier and not supported, a Stop-Control-Connection-Request SHOULD be sent to the peer and the originator moves into the wait_stop_reply state.
statements.trigger: Start-Control-Connection-Reply received with unsupported earlier version
statements.pre_cond: protocol.state = wait_ctl_reply & reply.version < request.version & reply.version.supported = false

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: In the event of a local termination, the originator MUST send a Stop-Control-Connection-Request and enter the wait_stop_reply state.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: If the originator receives a Stop-Control-Connection-Request it SHOULD send a Stop-Control-Connection-Reply and close the TCP connection making sure that the final TCP information has been "pushed" properly.
statements.post_cond: protocol.state = idle & tcp.connection = closed & tcp.data_pushed = true
actions: Ensure final TCP information is pushed properly

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: If a Stop-Control-Connection-Reply is received, the TCP connection SHOULD be closed and the control connection becomes idle.
actions: Transition control connection to idle state

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: If the version is earlier than the receiver's version and the earlier version can be supported by the receiver, the receiver SHOULD send a Start-Control-Connection-Reply.
statements.trigger: Start-Control-Connection-Request received with earlier but supported version
statements.pre_cond: receiver.state = idle & received.version < receiver.version & receiver.supports(received.version) = true

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: If the version is earlier than the receiver's version and the version cannot be supported, the receiver SHOULD send a Start-Connection-Reply message, close the TCP connection and remain in the idle state.
statements.trigger: Start-Control-Connection-Request received with unsupported earlier version
statements.pre_cond: receiver.state = idle & received.version < receiver.version & receiver.supports(received.version) = false

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: If the receiver's version is the same as earlier than the peer's, the receiver SHOULD send a Start-Control-Connection-Reply with the receiver's version and enter the established state.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: If the originator receives a Stop-Control-Connection-Request it SHOULD send a Stop-Control-Connection-Reply and close the TCP connection, making sure that the final TCP information has been "pushed" properly.
actions: ensure final TCP data is pushed

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: A PAC and PNS must have only one control connection between them.
actions: enforce single control connection per PAC-PNS pair

statements.subject: participant
statements.description: The winner MUST NOT send any messages on the connection the loser initiated.
actions: suppress all outbound PPTP control messages on loser-initiated TCP connection

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: A control connection SHOULD be closed by closing the underlying TCP connection under the following circumstances:

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: If a control connection is not in the established state (i.e., Start-Control-Connection-Request and Start-Control-Connection-Reply have not been exchanged), a control connection SHOULD be closed after 60 seconds by a peer waiting for a Start-Control-Connection-Request or Start-Control-Connection-Reply message.
statements.pre_cond: connection.state != established & (Start-Control-Connection-Request.received = false | Start-Control-Connection-Reply.received = false) & timer.elapsed >= 60
actions: close control connection by closing underlying TCP connection

statements.subject: peer
statements.description: If a peer's control connection is in the established state and has not received a control message for 60 seconds, it SHOULD send a Echo-Request message.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: If an Echo-Reply is not received 60 seconds after the Echo-Request message transmission, the control connection SHOULD be closed.
statements.pre_cond: connection.state = established & Echo-Request.sent = true & Echo-Reply.received = false & timer.echo_elapsed >= 60
actions: close control connection by closing underlying TCP connection

statements.subject: participant
statements.description: both the PNS and PAC should be implemented with multi-threaded architectures such that messages related to multiple calls are not serialized and blocked.

statements.subject: pptp
statements.description: The transit delay between the PAC and PNS should not exceed one second.

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: Establishing outbound international calls, including the modem training and negotiation sequences, may take in excess of 1 minute so the use of short timers is discouraged.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: If a state transition does not occur within 1 minute (except for connections in the idle or established states), the integrity of the protocol processing between the peers is suspect and the ENTIRE CONTROL CONNECTION should be closed and restarted.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: This Call ID value MUST be unique for the tunnel between the PNS and PAC to which it belongs.
actions: assign Call ID value that is unique within the tunnel between PNS and PAC

statements.subject: participant
statements.description: Modems should always indicate analog call type.

statements.subject: participant
statements.description: ISDN calls should indicate digital when unrestricted digital service or rate adaption is used and analog if digital modems are involved.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Dialing number, dialed number, and subaddress may be included in the message if they are available from the telephone network.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The PNS may choose not to accept the call if: -  No resources are available to handle more sessions -  The dialed, dialing, or subaddress fields are not indicative of an authorized user -  The bearer service is not authorized or supported
statements.pre_cond: pns.resources.available = false | pns.address.authorized = false | pns.bearer_service.authorized = false

statements.subject: session
statements.description: A final call connected message from the PAC to the PNS indicates that the call states for both the PAC and the PNS should enter the established state.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The call may be cleared following: An event on the telco connection. The PAC sends a Call-Disconnect-Notify message Receipt of a Call-Clear-Request.  The PAC sends a Call-Disconnect-Notify message A local reason. The PAC sends a Call-Disconnect-Notify message.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The PAC may send a Call-Disconnect-Notify to indicate that the incoming caller could not be connected.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The PAC MUST respond to the Outgoing-Call-Request message with an Outgoing-Call-Reply message once the PAC determines that: The call has been successfully connected A call failure has occurred for reasons such as: no interfaces are available for dial-out, the called party is busy or does not answer, or no dial tone is detected on the interface chosen for dialing

statements.subject: session
statements.description: If a Call-Clear-Request is received, the telco call SHOULD be released via appropriate mechanisms and a Call-Disconnect-Notify message SHOULD BE sent to the PNS.
actions: Release telco call via appropriate mechanisms

statements.subject: session
statements.description: If the call is disconnected by the client or by the telco interface, a Call-Disconnect-Notify message SHOULD be sent to the PNS.
statements.trigger: call disconnected by client or telco interface

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Flags (Bits 9-12) Must be set to zero (0).

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Ver (Bits 13-15) Must contain 1 (enhanced GRE).

statements.subject: pptp
statements.description: Although each side has indicated the maximum size of its receive window, it is recommended that a conservative approach be taken when beginning to transmit data.

statements.subject: pptp
statements.description: This situation should not arise if the sliding window procedures are being properly followed by the transmitter and receiver.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The PAC is not required to transmit multi-packet acknowledgments; it can instead acknowledge each packet individually as it is delivered to the PPP client.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The PAC acknowledges packet 4, and may assume packet 3 is lost.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: When the PAC does receive packet 3, it MUST not attempt to transmit it to the corresponding PPP client.
actions: do not forward out-of-sequence GRE packet to PPP client

statements.subject: message
statements.description: PPP does properly deal with the loss of packets, but not with reordering so out of sequence packets between the PNS and PAC MUST be silently discarded, or they may be reordered by the receiver.

statements.subject: pptp
statements.description: Packets with duplicate sequence numbers should never occur since the PAC and PNS never retransmit GRE packets.

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: PPTP requires that a time-out be used to recover from dropped data or acknowledgment packets.
actions: use time-out to recover from dropped data or acknowledgment packets

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: To reduce packet processing overhead, vendors may choose not to recompute the adaptive time-out for every received acknowledgment.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: For the PNS, this number should be small.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The PPD must be exchanged in the call connect sequences, even if it remains constant in an implementation.
actions: exchange PPD parameter during call connect sequences

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: PACFudge is not required but can be used to take overall processing overhead of the PAC into account.

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: When a time-out occurs, the time-out value should be adjusted rapidly upward.

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: Although the GRE packets are not retransmitted when a time-out occurs, the time-out should be adjusted up toward a maximum limit.

statements.subject: pptp
statements.description: To compensate for shifting internetwork time delays, a strategy must be employed to increase the time-out when it expires (notice that in addition to increasing the time-out, we are also shrinking the size of the window as described in the next section).
